This wizard will guide you through converting legacy property editors to their modern equivalents.
Choose how the converter should discover which document types and content to update.
Scans document types for properties using the legacy editor. Updates all matching document types, their data types, and all associated content. Document types with no content are also updated.
Fast — no content value scanning required.
Does not catch document types already updated by uSync whose content was never migrated.
Everything the Document type approach does, plus a direct scan of content values to find any unconverted data. Catches the uSync scenario and recovers from partial migration failures.
Finds unconverted content even when the document type schema was already updated.
Safe to run after a partial or failed migration to ensure nothing was missed.
Slower: scans actual content values in addition to the schema.
Analysing your content and document types…

Select the document types you want to convert. Unselected types will be skipped.

Runs the conversion without saving any changes. Use this to preview what would happen before committing.
Runs the actual conversion and saves all changes. Document types, data types, and content will be updated.
When enabled, the conversion will stop immediately if any item fails. When disabled, failed items will be logged and the conversion continues.
Runs a test conversion first without saving any changes. If the test succeeds, the actual conversion runs automatically. This takes longer but helps catch errors before modifying your data.
Only run a test conversion without saving any changes. Use this to preview what would happen before committing to the actual conversion.
When enabled, converted content nodes will be saved and published. When disabled (default), content is saved as a draft and must be published manually.
Choose a converter to start the conversion process.
